name: Question 4
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129388/assets/1bed15fe8f829f2a2248d5f366e4ca5df84274a767add87b3d26da9d3c2ab12d.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $x$-axis and the lines $y=x$ and $y=4-x$, as shown above. If the mass density function of $D$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=2x,$ find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,y\le x\le 4-y,\,\,0\le y\le 2\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129388/assets/fee47e2abe427ce056c77adb5df9a003263bade6e6e3e8d62ca789c162e2348c.png)

Using the formula for ${I}_{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y}^{4-y}{y}^{2}\cdot 2x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{y}^{4-y}2x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]_{x=y}^{x=4-y}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}(4-y)^{2}-{y}^{4}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}16{y}^{2}-8{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{16}{3}{y}^{3}-2{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{128}{3}-32 \\  & =\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

First, notice that D is a type II region with representation

D={(x,y):y≤x≤4−y,0≤y≤2},

as shown below.

Using the formula for Ix, we get

Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA=∫02∫y4−yy2⋅2xdxdy=∫02[∫y4−y2xy2dx]dy=∫02[x2y2]x=yx=4−ydx=∫02y2(4−y)2−y4dx=∫0216y2−8y3dy=[163y3−2y4]02=1283−32=323.
